title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
next_steps: Redwood to share latest perf spreadsheet and logs
Customer to run 24h stress test w/ new concurrency target
Schedule technical deep-dive for kernel/quantization options next Thurs
action_items: Tom Ellis - Share perf spreadsheet and raw run logs (due: 2026-07-02)
Priya Nair - Update batching policy YAML and push example config (due: 2026-07-03)
Raj Patel - Run 24h stress test on staging cluster and upload results (due: 2026-07-07)
Laura Gomez - Provide representative request trace and token distribution (due: 2026-07-01)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput optimizations. Reviewed recent benchmark runs, continuous batching behavior, and queueing/concurrency tuning. Identified mis-configured batching thresholds and a headroom goal to reach 1k rps under 200ms p95 for the 2k token average workload. Agreed on next steps: updated batching config, follow-up deep-dive on kernel/quantization, and a 24h stress run.
transcript:
00:00 Tom Ellis: ok everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, we are on for 45 minutes, quick agenda: run through the perf runs from last week, look at batching knobs, concurrency, and queue behavior, and define next steps.
00:12 Mike Chen: yeah thanks Tom, afternoon. quick high level, last week we saw a big jump in tokens per second after switching to the nightly build but latency got a bit spiky at peak.
00:27 Priya Nair: right, we ran the continuous batching patch — it reduces avg tokens/sec variance but if the concurrency is too low it queues up and you get p95 tail, basically a tradeoff between batching window and concurrency target.
00:44 Laura Gomez: we observed median latency 110ms but p95 hit 380ms during the 5pm surge, that was with 64 token avg payloads in the test, our real traffic is closer to 180-200 tokens.
01:02 Tom Ellis: okay, good data point, thanks. can you remind us of the target you gave in the doc? 1k rps with p95 under 200?
01:10 Mike Chen: yup that's the goal for peak for phase 1. ideally 200-250 token average.
01:18 Alex Duarte: we did two runs: run A used batching window 20ms and concurrency 32, run B used window 40ms concurrency 48. run A had lower latency at low load, run B got higher throughput but higher p95.
01:35 Raj Patel: small note, our staging GPUs are A100s, we plan to try H100 in prod; also we have network bursts pushed through a shared VPC so some noise is expected.
01:48 Priya Nair: also observed KV cash (sic) speedups when prefix cache hit rate above 60%, that reduces decode cost dramatically. might be a transcribe glitch, KV cache.
02:03 Laura Gomez: our token distribution has a long tail, a decent chunk of requests are 1.5k-2k tokens, which skews the batching behavior.
02:20 Tom Ellis: that matters a lot — continuous batching is most effective when request length distribution is tighter. recommendation: shard by length buckets or set a max batch token cap.
02:35 Mike Chen: shard by length sounds reasonable. any implications for memory on the GPU?
02:42 Priya Nair: yes if you allow big sequences you need to reserve KV cache and memory for the longest, that reduces effective batch size. we suggested two buckets: short (<256) and long (>=256) as a starting point.
03:02 Alex Duarte: quick recap of numbers: with two buckets, short path achieved ~1.1k rps at median 95ms, p95 170ms on A100 when concurrency=64 and batching window=30ms. long path held at ~140 rps with p95 480ms.
03:24 Laura Gomez: ok that aligns with our expectation. so to hit overall 1k rps we need better long-tail handling or more nodes.
03:35 Tom Ellis: yes, options: 1) increase concurrency and accept some p95 slippage 2) add dedicated pool for long sequences 3) quantize long-model variant to reduce memory and enable larger batch.
03:50 Mike Chen: we are sensitive to p95 because of SLAs. preferred is dedicated pool for long sequences if cost is manageable.
03:58 Priya Nair: from Redwood side we can provision a small dedicated pool for long-form and route via policy — keep short requests on shared host. routing policy is pretty straightforward.
04:10 Raj Patel: question on queueing — we saw request queue depth spike then system dropped packets, was that overload or our stress script?
04:20 Priya Nair: likely both; the runtime has a soft queue and when it exceeds a threshold new requests are rejected to protect latency. we can tune queue depth and provide backpressure to client.
04:33 Tom Ellis: we should model graceful degradation: queue threshold -> 429 with Retry-After, fallback to cached response if applicable.
04:43 Laura Gomez: will need to update client retry logic then, we have exponential backoff but need to honor Retry-After.
04:52 Alex Duarte: another practical win: tune the batching window dynamically by CPU/GPU utilization signals rather than static ms. we have an experimental adaptive window we can share.
05:06 Mike Chen: great — send that. also, are there kernel/quant options we should try? our infra team interested in int8 or 4-bit quantization variants.
05:18 Priya Nair: yes we have quantized variants; for long sequences int8 gets you memory headroom but latency profile varies. also some kernels on H100 are faster; will schedule a kernel/quant deep-dive.
05:33 Tom Ellis: action item to share perf spreadsheet and raw logs. Priya will drop updated batching YAML. Raj to run 24h stress test with the two-bucket config and concurrency targets we discussed.
05:48 Mike Chen: timeline wise we'd like results early next week so we can decide on Dedicated pool sizing.
05:55 Tom Ellis: noted. question on security/compliance: any requirements for logs or audit?
06:02 Raj Patel: we'll need to ensure logs exclude PII and meet SOC2 retention. also SSO with SAML in place for console access.
06:12 Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML SSO and can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping; we'll share the security docs link.
06:22 Sofia Ruiz: also product question — if we shard by length will it affect model consistency for chat history? some sessions switch between short and long.
06:33 Alex Duarte: good point — can route by conversation ID to preserve affinity, or fallback to the long pool when conversation exceeds threshold. we'll include recommendations in the doc.
06:48 Tom Ellis: ok wrapping up — quick recap of next steps and owners, then we'll open for questions.
06:56 Mike Chen: no further questions, thanks.
07:00 Tom Ellis: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with spreadsheet, configs, and schedule deep-dive for next Thurs.
07:08 END OF TRANSCRIPT
